title: Derived ringed-topos direct image preserves compatible central scalars
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Suppose given unital homomorphisms $s_A:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,A)$ and $s_B:R\to\Gamma(\mathcal D,B)$ whose restrictions $s_A(r)|_U\in A(U)$ and $s_B(r)|_V\in B(V)$ are central for every $r\in R$ and every site object $U\in\mathcal C$, $V\in\mathcal D$, and such that the structural map $c:u^{-1}A\to B$ carries $u^{-1}s_A(r)$ to $s_B(r)$ for every $r\in R$. On module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] define $(r f)_U(x)=s_A(r)|_U f_U(x)$, and likewise using $s_B$. Equip the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(A),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the induced $R$-linear structures [def-weil-linear-category, lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category]. The canonical K-injective derived direct image $Ru_*:D(B)\to D(A)$, computed with the derived-functor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. In particular it sends the endomorphism induced by the actual scalar section $s_B(r)$ to that induced by $s_A(r)$; no exactness of $u_*$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies), computation of the right derived functor on K-injectives. The compatible-central-scalar assertion is the implicit compatible-central-scalar prerequisite.

proof.text: For each module M construct the endomorphism multiplying its U-sections by s(r)_U. Centrality makes it module-linear, and compatibility of the section with restrictions makes it natural. The module axioms and ring homomorphism s give R → End(M). Restrict the canonical End(N)-module structure on Hom(M,N) along this map. Naturality of scalar endomorphisms proves both scalar-composition laws. This constructs LA and LB with exactly the required evaluation formulas.

For the underlying set sheaf T of u_*M, let z₀:T→T be the zero generalized element. Apply module_linear with the constant unit section and x=y=z=z₀. Preservation of one gives transpose(z₀)=transpose(z₀)+transpose(z₀), so cancellation gives transpose(z₀)=0. Next apply module_linear with the constant section s_A(r), x=id, y=z₀ and z=multiplication by s_A(r). Compatibility identifies the scalar after inverse image with s_B(r). Naturality of the underlying comparison and of the adjunction identifies u_*(r id_M) with r id_(u_*M). The scalar-identity criterion for linear functors proves underived linearity; additivity is a field of the ringed-topos morphism.

The module category over B is Grothendieck abelian. The existing Grothendieck K-injective resolution instance gives, for every complex N, a quasi-isomorphism N→I with I K-injective. Only this part of the stronger functorial degreewise-injective resolution theorem is needed. Use this enough hypothesis in the existing canonical rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions construction.

Give the type of K-injective complexes the category induced by their images in the homotopy category. Let L be its inclusion followed by Qh. The Hom bijection into a K-injective target proves L is full. Resolve a chosen complex representative of each derived object; the resolution quasi-isomorphism and quotientCompQhIso show that L is essentially surjective.

The derived unit, restricted to K-injective complexes, is an isomorphism from the restriction of F.mapHomotopyCategory ⋙ Qh to L ⋙ RF. The former is additive and R-linear by the underived scalar calculation and the linearity of the homotopy and derived localizations. Transport these properties along the unit isomorphism, then descend them along the full essentially surjective L using Mathlib Functor.additive_of_full_essSurj_comp and Functor.linear_of_full_essSurj_comp. This proves additivity and linearity of exactly the canonical RF, without choosing any new derived functor or using exactness of the module direct image.

Apply linearity to r times the identity and use preservation of identities. The evaluation formulas defining LA and LB identify these scalar maps with multiplication by the actual compatible sections.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q78-61bbf851f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all 11 cited statements and the sources. Verdict PASS, with no changes. Shape: one commit; item still unsplit on side-live, not on the dropped list, no repair note, no new nodes. Statement correction: the delivery adds local centrality of s_A(r)|_U and s_B(r)|_V. It is necessary, because the ringed-topos and module definitions allow noncommutative rings. I rechecked the counterexample on a point topos with A=B=M_2(Q) and t↦diag(1,0): t·id is not A-linear (d·E12=E12 but E12·d=0). The only citer, lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor, uses commutative coefficient sheaves, so it still holds. Steps: (1) the sectionwise R-linear category uses centrality; (2) the transpose formula of def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, with letters reversed, plus c(u^{-1}s_A)=s_B gives F(rf)=rF(f). (3) Mod(B) is Grothendieck by the noncommutative ring-sheaf node; K-injective resolutions exist; Q_A F_K is exact by the cone/biproduct argument; 070K (derived.tex l.9767, read) gives RF. (4) The map-computation node's RF is def-sfb-right-derived-functor, which is defined through the same lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived, so it is the same canonical Ru_*. (5) Uniqueness of the homotopy class, linearity of Q and cancelling the fixed c_a, c_b give additivity and R-linearity of Ru_*. (6) Scalar endomorphisms go to scalar endomorphisms. Edge cases r=0, r=1, R=0 and unbounded complexes are fine. Duplicates: lem-sbc-ambient-operations-scalar-linearity is only the pro-étale, commutative-ring version, and lem-cbc-exact-linear-derived-functor needs F exact; neither restates the item. I accept the three declared tool uses: the noncommutative Grothendieck node, the 070K total-derived node and the ringed-topos definition. No SGA source is used. lean.statement: theorem ringedDerivedPushforward_linear {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D} (A : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}) (B : Sheaf K RingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ringedSiteModules.{u} A)] [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (ringedSiteModules.{u} B)] (u : RingedToposMorphism B A) (R : Type v) [CommRing R] (sA : R →+* RingCat.sectionsSubring A.obj) (sB : R →+* RingCat.sectionsSubring B.obj) (centralA : ∀ (r : R) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a : A.obj.obj U), (sA r).val U * a = a * (sA r).val U) (centralB : ∀ (r : R) (V : Dᵒᵖ) (b : B.obj.obj V), (sB r).val V * b = b * (sB r).val V) (compatible : ∀ (r : R) (T : Sheaf J (Type u)) (z : T ⟶ (sheafCompose J (forget RingCat)).obj A), (∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (t : T.obj.obj U), z.hom.app U t = (sA r).val U) → ∀ (V : Dᵒᵖ) (t : (u.inverse.obj T).obj.obj V), ((u.inverse.map z) ≫ u.ringMap).hom.app V t = (sB r).val V) : ∃ (LA : Linear R (ringedSiteModules.{u} A)) (LB : Linear R (ringedSiteModules.{u} B)) (enough : ∀ N : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u} B) ℤ, ∃ (I : CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u} B) ℤ) (a : N ⟶ I), I.IsKInjective ∧ QuasiIso a), (fun [_iA : Linear R (ringedSiteModules.{u} A)] [_iB : Linear R (ringedSiteModules.{u} B)] ↦ (∀ (M N : ringedSiteModules.{u} A) (f : M ⟶ N) (r : R) (U : Cᵒᵖ) (x : M.val.obj U), (r • f).val.app U x = (sA r).val U • f.val.app U x) ∧ (∀ (M N : ringedSiteModules.{u} B) (f : M ⟶ N) (r : R) (V : Dᵒᵖ) (x : M.val.obj V), (r • f).val.app V x = (sB r).val V • f.val.app V x) ∧ (u.modules.rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions enough).Additive ∧ Functor.Linear R (u.modules.rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions enough) ∧ (∀ (N : DerivedCategory (ringedSiteModules.{u} B)) (r : R), (u.modules.rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions enough).map (r • 𝟙 N) = r • 𝟙 ((u.modules.rightDerivedFunctorOfQuasiIsoResolutions enough).obj N))) (_iA := LA) (_iB := LB)
